notes.decision: Rendered ⲧⲟⲛⲱ as 'weighty matter' per accumulated vocabulary entry (which notes ⲧⲟⲛⲱ as substantival 'raising-up' = 'weighty/momentous thing'). The qualitative ϩⲧⲁⲓⲁⲓⲧ I read as Lyc. reflex of ⲧⲁⲩⲏⲩ 'has been proclaimed/sent forth' (qualitative of ⲧⲁⲩⲟ 'proclaim'); fits the discourse since the disciple is asking about a saying he has heard. Alternative reading: stative of ⲁⲓⲁⲓ 'multiply' = 'has grown great' is also plausible.

Greek προσχαρίζομαι 'grant in addition' — distinguished from simple ⲭⲁⲣⲓⲍⲉ in line 18. The προσ- prefix is theologically significant: when one prays for another, the granting is supererogatory (in addition to the regular reckoning). This reconciles the maxim of line 9 with the efficacy of intercessory prayer.

Translated 'this prayer came into being from the firsts' — ⲛ̄ⲧⲍⲟⲩⲓⲧⲉ from ⲡⲍⲟⲩⲓ̈ⲧ 'the foremost/first' (in glossary). The Apostle grounds prayer's efficacy in cosmogonic precedence: prayer's reality comes from the original cosmic beings.

'(The Church) which bears the flesh' — Greek φορεῖ 'wear, bear (as garment).' The Church-on-earth is characterized as the flesh-bearing community, distinguishing it from the cosmic divine assemblies but parallel in its prayer-function.

Final-line verbs all 3sg.f perfect, subject = the Mother of Life from line 29-30. The triple sequence beseeched/glorified/blessed (with restored ⲁⲥⲁⲓⲧⲓ 'requested,' ⲁⲥϣⲗⲏⲛ 'prayed' preceding) gives the Mother's fivefold cosmogonic prayer-act — paralleling the gods' first prayer in line 21 and grounding the teaching that all prayer descends from primordial divine prayer.

Translated 'the first standing-fast' preserving the verbal-spatial nominalization of ⲧⲱⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧ⸗ 'stand fast,' attested in glossary as a substantival cosmic title (cf. ⲡⲧⲱⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧϩ 'the standing-fast / the establishment'). The Father is here identified as the foundational standing — first in a series presumably continued through the Living Spirit and other emanations.

Rendered 'the petition.' The form is unusual; in context (governed by relative ⲉⲧⲁⲥⲥⲁⲡⲥⲧ̄ 'which she had supplicated him for') it functions as the cognate object of ⲥⲱⲡⲥ̄ 'petition.' Possibly a Lycopolitan substantival form of ⲥⲱⲡⲥ̄, or alternatively cognate with ⲥⲟⲉⲓⲧ 'cry, report.' Confidence moderate.

Translated 'the first Expander.' Compound: ⲣⲉϥ- ('one who does') + ϯ ('give') + ⲟⲩⲁⲥⲧⲛ̄ ('expanse, breadth' — cf. accumulated ⲟⲩⲉⲥⲧⲁⲛⲧ 'wide/broad'). Standard agentive formation paralleling ⲣⲉϩ†ⲥⲃⲱ 'teacher.' The epithet is confirmed by line 28-29 ⲁϩϯⲟⲩⲁⲥⲧⲛ̄ ⲛⲉϩ ⲍⲛ̄ ⲧⲭⲱⲣⲁ ⲙ̄ⲡⲙ̄ⲧⲁⲛ 'and gave him expanse in the country of rest' — the Living Spirit's defining cosmic act. 'Expander' preserves the active verbal-emission semantics required by the correspondential principle.

Translated 'struck him down.' The verb is from the same root as accumulated ⲃⲁⲡϩ 'to be struck down/defeated' (used of the dark powers' defeat). Here in active form with 3sg.m suffix; the object 'him' must refer to the dark adversary that had weakened the First Man (referenced by ⲛ̄ⲧⲁϩⲣ̄ⲃⲱⲃ 'because he had been weakened' immediately preceding). The sequence then continues with the Living Spirit's rescue of the First Man (took him in, released him, set him on his feet, gave him expanse).

Rendered 'a binding.' In context the First Man finds himself 'in the midst of the encampment of demons, a ⲧⲱⲃϥ̄ of the powers of the Devil' — in apposition with the previous loci of imprisonment. Most plausibly from ⲧⲱⲃⲉ 'seal, bind' with 3sg.m suffix, hence 'a sealing/binding of him by the powers of the Devil.' Distinct from the homograph ⲧⲱⲃⲍ̄ 'pray' used elsewhere on the page. Confidence moderate.

Translated 'and he joined himself to the Mother of Life.' ⲧⲟⲩⲓ̈ⲁϩ likely a Lycopolitan reflex of ⲧⲟⲩⲱϩ 'add, join, attach.' The First Man's pre-cosmic conjunction with the Mother of Life (before his descent) is a standard Manichaean cosmogonic moment.

This kephalaion appears to recapitulate the cosmogonic narrative of the First Man's rescue — the Mother of Life's intercessory prayer, the Father's response, the Living Spirit's descent, and the rescue from the Deep — in preparation for an enumeration of the cosmic 'standing-fasts' (Father = first; Living Spirit = (third?), apparently associated with the ὑποδοχεύς 'receiver' in line 31). The damaged final lines suggest a typology comparing emanations.
ⲟⲩⲛⲁⲟ = indefinite article + ⲛⲁⲟ 'great' (= ⲛⲟϭ). With ⲛⲟⲁⲙ 'might/power' (in glossary): 'a great might.' Direct attributive construction.

Recurring key term throughout this page (16+ occurrences). Lycopolitan ⲧⲱⲃⲥ̄ = Sahidic ⲧⲱⲃϩ̄ 'pray, beseech, exhort, intercede, advocate' (regular Lyc. ⲥ for ϩ). Both nominal and verbal usage. Translated consistently as 'intercession' (noun) and 'intercede' (verb) to capture the prayer-on-behalf-of dimension central to the Mother of Life's role for the First Man and the Church's role for departing catechumens. Cf. accumulated vocabulary entry ⲧⲧⲱⲃⲍ 'I beseech.'

Parsed as ⲁϩ- (Lyc. purpose-infinitive prefix = Sah. ⲉ-ⲧⲣⲉ-) + ⲧⲟⲩⲓ̈ + 3sg.m. suffix -ⲁϩ = 'in order to raise him.' From ⲧⲟⲩⲱ 'raise' (per terminology guide, vertical-soteriological semantics preserved). The Mother's act of raising the First Man, paralleling the Manichaean cosmogonic motif.

Abstract ⲙⲛⲧ- + ⲟⲱⲃ. Likely related to ⲡⲉⲧⲁⲟⲃⲉ 'the abomination/foul thing' (in glossary). Translated 'foulness' (= abomination-state) paired antithetically with ⲡⲧⲉⲕⲟ 'destruction' as the dual designation of the place into which the First Man descends. Confidence moderate; the lexeme is rare.

From ⲟⲩⲱⲥⲧⲛ 'be wide, spread' (cf. accumulated ⲟⲩⲉⲥⲧⲁⲛⲧ 'wide/broad' qualitative). Substantival 'wideness, spaciousness, room.' The First Man is to be given 'room/space forth' from the cosmic prison-system — a release-figure paralleling ⲃⲱⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ.

Tentatively read as Lyc. variant of ⲥⲱϣⲛϩ 'labor, distress, struggle' (Crum). With preceding [ⲥⲁ-] (line 6 restoration): 'after toil unto eternity' — fits the eschatological rest-after-labor topos. Could alternatively read as ⲥⲧⲱⲛⲉⲥ or related lexeme. Confidence moderate.

Recurring term (lines 8, 23, and restored 29). Likely Lycopolitan reflex of ϩⲁⲏ 'end, last' with prosthetic ϣ- and final -ⲁ — possibly a Manichaean technical noun for the cosmic 'consummation' or moment of completion. Confirmed by context: 'the Five stood at the ⲡϣⲁⲏⲁ' = 'the Five stood at the consummation' (line 23). Translated consistently as 'consummation.' Distinct from accumulated ⲡⲓⲃⲱⲗⲟⲥ ⲛ̄ⲍⲁⲉ 'last bōlos' and ⲡⲥⲏⲩ ⲛ̄ⲧⲍⲁⲏ 'time of the end.'

Difficult clause. Parsed as: ⲉⲧⲁⲥ- (relative perfect, fem. subject = the Mother from prior context) + ⲧⲱⲃⲥ + ⲡⲓⲱⲧ ⲙⲙⲁϩ in apposition. ⲙⲙⲁϩ here = 'in him' (locative). Translation: 'with which she interceded — the Father (being) in him.' Captures the Manichaean theological structure where the Mother's intercession brings the indwelling Father-presence into the First Man. Alternative parsing 'with which the Father interceded for him' would require subject-suffix mismatch.

Lyc. plural ⲛⲉϩ- + ⲧⲱⲟⲥ 'mountain' (cf. accumulated ⲧⲱⲟⲥ 'mountains/regions,' Lyc. plural of ⲧⲟⲟⲩ). Translated 'mountains' as cosmic structural element in inventory with firmaments, wheels, ships, bones, preparations, strongholds. Standard Manichaean cosmographic vocabulary.

notes.coptic_form: ⲡⲛⲁⲟ̄ ⲙⲡ̄ⲛⲁ ... ⲡⲙⲉⲣⲓⲧ ⲛⲛⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲛⲉ ... ⲡⲛⲁⲟ̄ ⲛⲉⲕⲱⲧ ... ⲡⲓⲡⲛⲁ̄ ⲉⲧⲁⲛⲥ̄ ... ⲡϣⲁⲣⲡ ⲛⲣⲱⲙⲉ
notes.decision: These five named figures (Great One of the Spirit, Beloved of the Lights, Great Builder, Living Spirit, First Man) constitute the Five Greatnesses (ⲧϯⲟⲩ ⲙ̄ⲙⲛ̄ⲧⲛⲁⲅ in glossary) standing at the cosmic consummation. The 'these Five' (ⲡⲓϯⲟⲩ) in line 23 confirms this enumeration. Note: the Great One of the Spirit and the Living Spirit may be coreferent here, or together count as one of the Five Fathers.

Substantival use: 'the First Standing-Fast' = the foremost-established one = the First Man. Built on ⲡⲧⲱⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧϩ 'the standing-fast/establishment' (in glossary). Refers back to the First Man as the foundational standing of the cosmic order.

Parsed as relative perfect 3sg.f ⲧⲉⲧⲁ- + ⲥⲉ (rise/stand, Lyc. variant) + ⲁⲣⲉⲧⲥ̄ 'on her feet.' = 'she who has stood up on her feet.' Subject is the Living Soul (ⲧⲓⲩⲭⲏ ⲉⲧⲁⲛⲥ̄), feminine. The Soul-substance erected throughout the cosmos awaiting purification.

End of page; ⲛ̄ⲧⲉϩ likely Lyc. possessive 'of his' (= ⲛⲧⲉϥ) with the noun continuing on next page. Translated 'in the power of his …' to mark the page-boundary continuation. Could alternatively be the start of a compound noun ⲛⲧⲉϩ-X where X is lost.

Treating the editor's single-letter restoration [ⲙ] at the start of line 1 as part of certain text. The remainder of ⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁϭ ('Greatness,' = ⲧⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁⲟ̄ in Lyc glossary) is preserved; the ⲙ is securely restored from context. Single-letter restorations completing obvious words are treated as certain throughout this page per pragmatic editorial choice. The word likely continues from a phrase on the prior page (e.g., 'the Son of/the Power of/the Ambassador of [the] Greatness'); the visible noun functions as predicate genitive of an unnamed subject — the Ambassador per the chapter context (line 6).

The word ⲙⲛⲧⲁϣⲗⲣⲉ (split across lines 2-3) is an unidentified abstract noun. Possibilities include: (a) a Lyc form related to ϣⲗⲏⲗ 'pray' giving 'prayer-state' (fitting the chapter's prayer theme); (b) a form related to ϣⲏⲣⲉ 'child' giving 'sonship/childhood' (fitting the works of the Five Sons); (c) a privative ⲙⲛⲧ-ⲁⲧ-X. Translated as '[X]hood' pending parallels.

ⲡⲓⲉⲙⲛⲧⲉ = 'this Hades/Underworld' (= ⲁⲙⲛⲧⲉ, Lyc with prosthetic ⲉ-). In Manichaean cosmology this names the lower realm of death and oppression where the soul is bound. ϣⲁⲭⲍ is a qualitative of uncertain root — possibly related to ϣⲱϫⲉ 'destroy/burn' or ϣⲱϫϩ 'be afflicted' — giving 'harsh/scorching/painful.' The pairing with 'oppression' (ⲑⲗⲓⲃⲉ) and 'lower side' (ⲡⲥⲁⲙⲡⲓⲧⲛⲉ) supports a sense of harshness or scorching.

Qualitative of ⲙⲟⲩϫⲧ̄/ⲙⲟⲩⲝⲧ̄ 'mingle, be kneaded together' (in glossary) — the soul 'while being mingled in them' (the fleshes of death). Standard Manichaean cosmogonic-anthropological vocabulary for the entanglement of light-substance with dark matter.

From ⲟⲩⲱⲥⲧⲛ̄ 'be wide, spread' (cf. ⲟⲩⲉⲥⲧⲁⲛⲧ 'wide/broad' in glossary). Causative: 'he made (her) wide,' 'he gave wideness/relief.' Soteriological liberation expressed spatially as the giving-of-room.

Apparent variant of ⲡⲱⲕ ⲛⲍⲏⲧ 'purpose of heart' (in glossary) — the third instance in this passage's enumeration (lines 12-13 ⲡⲱⲕ ⲛ̄|ⲍⲏⲧ; line 16 ⲡⲱⲛⲕ ⲛⲍⲏⲧ). The ⲛ̄ may be a scribal slip or a Lyc variant stem. Translated identically as 'purpose of heart.' Could alternatively reflect ⲡⲱⲛⲕ 'scoop/draw out' (ⲡⲱⲛⲕ ⲛ̄ϩⲏⲧ = 'drawing-forth of heart'), but consistency with lines 12-13 favors 'purpose.'

Lexeme not securely identifiable. The form ⲁϥⲡ̄ⲟⲇⲟ (with possible word-internal break ⲡ̄ ⲟⲇⲟ in transcription) is likely a verb of motion/conveyance. Possibilities: (a) Greek προοδέω/πρόοδος 'advance, lead forth'; (b) Coptic ⲡⲱⲱⲇⲉ 'leap, pass over'; (c) Greek πηδάω 'leap'; (d) ⲡⲱⲧ 'run' in some extended form. The collocation ⲍⲓ ⲍⲟⲩⲓⲧ 'as foremost' and directional ⲁ-ⲡⲥⲱⲙⲁ ⲧⲏⲣϥ 'to the whole body' supports a sense of leading-forth as guide. Translated 'led-forth as foremost' tentatively. Flagged as proposed term.

1sg perfect of ⲧⲟⲩⲛⲟⲥ 'raise, awaken' (cf. ⲣⲉϩⲧⲟⲩⲛⲟⲩⲥ 'the Awakener' in glossary) with 2sg.m suffix -ⲉⲧⲕ — 'I have raised you up forth.' Apostolic-soteriological speech: the Ambassador addresses the soul/disciple as having been raised. Per terminology guide, ⲧⲟⲩⲛⲟⲥ-class verbs preserve vertical-soteriological semantics; rendered 'raised up forth.'
Circumstantial + ⲥⲱⲡⲥ̄ 'beseech, entreat' with 3sg.f object suffix -ⲥ̄ — 'beseeching her' (the prayer/the soul). The prayer is here treated as feminine, parallel to the soul (ϯⲩⲭⲏ).

Likely scribal/dialectal for ⲁⲗⲗⲁ ⲙⲁⲣⲛ̄ⲉⲓ 'but let us come' — concessive ⲁⲗⲗⲁ + 1pl jussive ⲙⲁⲣⲛ̄- + ⲉⲓ 'come.' Standard Coptic exhortation introducing a new section. The doubled ⲗ-onset and ⲣ for ⲙⲁⲣ may reflect Lyc orthographic features or scribal compression.
Translated as 'he stood fast' per the standard idiom ⲧⲱⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧ⸗ (in glossary). The 3sg.m perfect ⲁϩ-ⲧⲱⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧϥ̄ refers to a male subject established firmly.
Restored 'the First Man' per editor and standard Manichaean cosmogonic figure (in glossary). The presence of this title plus ⲡⲣⲉⲥⲃⲉⲩⲧⲏⲥ in line 23 suggests the page is treating cosmic figures.
Translated as 'prayer/beseech' — same root recurs in lines 17, 18 (ⲧⲱⲃϩ ... ⲁⲥⲧⲱⲃϩ 'she prayed'), suggesting a recurring theme of prayer/petition in this damaged passage.
'Ambassador' — the Third Ambassador, standard Manichaean title (Greek πρεσβευτής, in glossary). The free-standing occurrence here likely identifies the cosmic agent in view.

Translated 'the Living Ones' per accumulated vocabulary (ⲡⲏⲓ̈ ⲛⲛⲉⲧⲁⲛⲍ̄ 'the house of the Living Ones'). The substantive participle/relative on ⲱⲛⲍ̄ 'live' is standard Manichaean cosmological designation.

Read as Lycopolitan reflex of ϩⲱⲱϥ 'himself, also' (cf. accumulated dialect note ⲍⲱⲱϩ = ϩⲱⲱϥ). The form ⲍⲱⲙϩ shows additional dialectal/scribal variation. Translated 'himself' as intensive pronoun applied to Jesus.
Lycopolitan ⲝ for ϫ; ⲝⲱⲕ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ = standard ϫⲱⲕ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'complete, fulfill, perfect.' Imperative or infinitive force depending on syntax; rendered 'complete' as best general gloss.

Likely Lycopolitan relative perfect ⲉⲧⲁϥ- + verb stem in ⲭ-, possibly ⲉⲧⲁϥϫ- 'who has done/said/given/etc.' Insufficient context to determine root. Left as transliteration plus 'who has' relative marker.

Lycopolitan perfect 3sg ⲁϥϯ 'he gave' (ⲁϩ for ⲁϥ + ϯ 'give'). Confirmed by following indirect object ⲛⲉⲩ 'to them' and direct object ⲡⲱⲕ ⲛ̄ⲍⲏⲧ 'the purpose of heart.' Echoes the same construction in line 3 (he gave them the hope) — gift-giving formula.

Verbal compound of unclear root + ⲁϩⲉⲉϥ (likely ⲁϥⲁϩⲉ-ⲉϥ or ⲁϥⲱϩⲉ qualitative + suffix) followed by ⲛ̄ⲣⲙⲍⲉ 'as freeman.' The construction ⲁϩⲉ-ⲉϥ ⲛ̄- 'stand him as / make him to be' fits the freedom-bestowal context (cf. accumulated ⲣⲙⲍⲉ 'freeman'). Tentative rendering 'they made him stand as freeman.'
Lycopolitan possessive ⲛⲉϩ- 'his' (cf. accumulated ⲡⲉϩ-) + ⲭⲁⲭⲉ (Lyc. ⲭ for ϫ) = ϫⲁϫⲉ 'enemy.' Plural 'his enemies.'
Lycopolitan perfect ⲁϥϫⲓ 'he received' (ⲁϩ for ⲁϥ; ⲭ for ϫ). The receipt of ⲧⲍⲉⲗⲡⲓⲥ 'the hope' parallels line 3's giving of hope — likely the same Manichaean topos of Jesus bestowing hope on Adam.
ⲧⲍⲉ = ⲧϩⲉ 'the manner, thus' (regular Lyc. ⲍ for ϩ). The phrase ⲧⲍⲉ ⲁⲛ ⲧⲉ ⲧⲉⲓ 'thus also is this' is standard Coptic comparative-typological discourse-marker.
Lycopolitan 2pl conjunctive/circumstantial of ⲧⲱⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧ⸗ 'stand fast' (in glossary as ⲧⲏⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧ⸗). Direct address to disciples: 'you (pl.) stand fast.'

Imperative-of-result formula 'become you knowing' = 'know!' / 'be it known to you' (cf. accumulated ⲱⲱⲡⲉ ⲉⲧⲉⲧⲛ̄ⲥⲁⲩⲛⲉ — same construction in 2pl). Standard Manichaean teacher-formula opening expositions.
Read as Lycopolitan perfect ⲁϥⲣ̄- + Greek loanword ⲁⲓⲥⲑⲁⲛⲉ < αἰσθάνεσθαι 'perceive by sense.' The ⲁϩ for ⲁϥ is regular Lyc. orthography (cf. ⲁϩϯ in line 8). Rendered 'he perceived' (perfect tense).
Lycopolitan ⲍⲃⲏⲩⲉ = ϩⲃⲏⲩⲉ 'works' (regular Lyc. ⲍ for ϩ; plural of ϩⲱⲃ). With genitive ⲛ̄- = 'of (the) works.'
Compound preposition ϣⲁ-ⲍⲟⲩⲛ 'unto-the-inside' + ⲁⲣⲁϩ 'to him.' Lyc. ⲍⲟⲩⲛ = Sah. ϩⲟⲩⲛ. Spatial-directional 'inward unto him.'

Per accumulated vocabulary: tentatively 'unto him' (compound preposition with 3sg.m. suffix) or 'unto fullness/completion.' Either fits a closing formula. Without surrounding context, rendered conservatively 'unto him.'

Translated as 'has reckoned/has set' — qualitative perfect of ⲱⲡ 'count, reckon, account.' The verb takes a direct object (this rest, a remembrance) consistently across the page, fitting the ecclesiological semantic field of 'establishing/reckoning' a remembrance for the deceased catechumen. Also functions intransitively as 'be reckoned to' (line 4 pattern). Same root as ⲡⲣ̄ⲡⲙⲉⲩⲉ 'make remembrance' in glossary, here as an alternate verb of cultic-commemorative action.

Translated 'his four great gates' (preserving the ms glyph ⲋ as written). The ⲋ in this manuscript appears to function as a variant for ϭ; ⲛⲁⲋ = ⲛⲁϭ 'great' and ⲋⲣⲟ likely = ϭⲣⲟ, an unusual Lycopolitan/Manichaean form of ⲣⲟ 'gate.' Confirmed by line 17 'third gate (ⲋⲣⲟ)' as section-marker pointing to a soteriological/structural enumeration of four 'gates' through which the catechumen passes. Alternative reading 'victories' (= ϫⲣⲟ) less likely given the structural-enumerative function.
Parsed as ⲛ̄ⲧⲉ ϩⲛ̄ ⲁⲓ ϭⲉ 'from these things, therefore' — closing the first section before the leer break. ⲁⲓ = Lyc. demonstrative 'these'; ϭⲉ = particle 'therefore.' Reading uncertain.

'The second' — Lycopolitan feminine ordinal ⲙⲁⲍ-ⲥⲛⲧⲉ marking the section division. Continued by 'The third (ⲡⲙⲁⲍϣⲁⲙⲧ)' at line 17, confirming the kephalaion's enumerative structure of four 'gates' (per line 7).

Translated 'for the man's portion' tentatively, reading ⲡⲁⲥ as Lyc. variant of ⲡⲁⲥⲉ 'half, share, portion.' The double-marker ⲙ̄ⲡⲁⲥ ⲙⲧⲣⲱⲙⲉ = 'for-his-portion of-the-man.' Could alternatively be a scribal redundancy or an unidentified pronominal form. Confidence low.

Translated 'she habitually washes' — habitual ϣⲁⲥ- + ⲭⲱⲃⲉ. The verb fits the soul-purification context (paired with ⲧⲟⲩⲃⲟ 'be purified'). Could alternatively be ϣⲱⲃⲉ 'change, exchange.' Going with the washing/cleansing register that matches the surrounding language of purification.

Translated 'his kin/relation' tentatively — fits the kinship-list context (father, mother, son, daughter, kinsman). The lexeme ⲥⲁⲩⲧ is unidentified; possibly Lyc. variant of ⲥⲟⲉⲓⲧ 'fame/report' or an unattested kinship-term. Confidence low.
Translated 'I marvel/am amazed' — ϯ-ⲱⲁⲡⲧ as 1sg present of a verb related to ϣⲡⲏⲣⲉ 'wonder.' The doubled ⲧ̄ⲧ may be scribal or a Lyc. orthographic feature.

Translated 'she habitually ripens forth' per accumulated glossary entry ϣⲃⲱⲛ 'ripening (tentative)' and the cosmological-soteriological context of the soul's gradual purification 'until this end.' The maturation/release sense fits the eschatological framework.
Lyc qualitative 'narrow/oppressed' (per accumulated vocabulary). Could refer to the catechumen's narrow path or to the affliction his soul undergoes.
Greek loanword συγγενής 'kinsman, blood-relation.' Recurs in line 24 in similar damaged context, suggesting the kinsman-intercession motif structures this kephalaion.

Substantival qualitative on ⲭⲁⲗⲭ 'mingle, fashion together' (in glossary): 'the one who is mingled.' Refers either to the catechumen (whose soul is mingled with cosmic Light) or to Christ-as-Mingled. The pairing with 'man who lives' (ⲡⲣⲱⲙⲉ ⲉⲧⲁⲛⲋ) suggests the catechumen's living-but-bound condition awaiting redemption.
Standard Manichaean soteriological phrase 'redemption of the soul.' Confirms this kephalaion's theme: the catechumen's soul-redemption through prayer and kinsman-intercession.
ϣⲛⲋⲧⲏⲩ = ϣⲛ̄-ϩⲧⲏⲩ 'compassionate, merciful' (lit. 'become-of-pity-of-heart'). Modifies 'the light' — the merciful Light, possibly the Light-Mind or the Form of Light that comes for the released soul.

ϯ as feminine article + ⲟⲩⲁⲥⲧⲛ qualitative 'wide/broad' substantivized = 'the breadth/wideness'; ⲡⲉϩⲛⲁ likely 'his pity/mercy' (ⲛⲁ from ⲛⲁⲉ family in glossary). 'The wideness of his mercy' fits the soteriological context. Alternatively could be incomplete word with line-break (cf. ⲡⲁ|ⲧⲏⲙⲁ in line 19).
Lyc form for ⲉϫⲛ̄ 'upon, for, concerning' or ϩⲁ-ϫⲛ̄ 'for, on behalf of.' Standard prepositional usage: 'prayed concerning/for the soul.' The double ⲭⲁⲭ is dialectal.
Parsed as ⲉⲧⲁⲥ-ⲉ(ⲓ) ⲁⲃⲁⲗ '(soul) which has come forth' — the redeemed soul that has emerged from the cosmos through the catechumen's prayer.
Habitual 3pl 'they (habitually) release her forth from the affliction.' Subject likely the angels/redeemers who release the soul from cosmic bondage. ⲃⲱⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ = 'release' per accumulated terminology.

ϣⲁ ⲁⲛⲏⲍⲉ = 'unto eternity, forever' (cf. accumulated ϣⲁⲁⲛⲏⲍⲉ). Closes the doxological-soteriological clause about the redeemed soul. The leer marks paragraph break before the new section's parable of the bound man.

Doublet of perfect-3pl punitive verbs: 'they scourged him, they bound him' (ⲉϣⲧ 'scourge/afflict' per accumulated entry; ⲙⲁⲣϩ̄ from ⲙⲟⲩⲣ 'bind'). The judicial sequence describing what worldly authorities do to a sinner — allegorical for the cosmic judgment of the catechumen who sins.

notes.coptic_form: ⲏ ⲡⲉϩⲱⲧ ⲏ ⲡⲉϩⲥⲁⲛ ⲧⲱⲛⲉ ⲛ̄ϩⲃⲱⲕ
notes.decision: 'Either his father or his brother arose to go.' The kinsman-rescue scenario: a family member rises to journey on behalf of the bound man — providing the worldly typos for cosmic intercession (apostle/elect-as-spiritual-kinsman).

Greek loanword ὑπόσχεσις 'pledge, promise, undertaking.' The kinsman gives a pledge (= surety/bail) for the bound man's life. Allegorically: the prayer/pledge offered for the bound catechumen's soul-redemption.

'The master who has bound (him).' δεσπότης here names the cosmic-judicial authority who has bound the sinner — paralleling the Judge of cosmos in earlier Kephalaia. Standard Manichaean cosmographic register.

ⲫⲟⲥ at line-start is a partial trace of an unknown preceding word (perhaps ending in -φῶς 'light' or a Greek compound). ⲡⲙⲏⲧ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ likely 'the midst forth' (= ⲡⲙⲏⲧⲉ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ). ⲡⲁⲛⲭⲱⲭ 'wellspring/source' (in glossary) — the cosmic source of evil from which the binding originates, in eschatological inversion.

The character + recurs throughout this page (lines 8, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22 [ⲛⲥⲧ-], 24, 27, 28, 29) as an editorial mark in the transcription representing letters resolved contextually. In ⲯⲩⲭⲏ contexts (++ⲩⲭⲏ, +ⲩⲭⲏ) the second + represents ⲯ; preceding +-marks represent the genitive ⲛ̄ or article ⲧ-/ⲡ-. In line 18 ϣⲁⲩ+ⲟⲩⲱ resolves to ϣⲁⲩⲧⲟⲩⲱ 'they habitually raise' (per terminology rule, ⲧⲟⲩⲱ MUST be 'raise' preserving vertical-soteriological semantics). I preserve + literally in the Coptic field and translate based on resolved context.

Lexeme of uncertain identity. Likely Greek loanword μνεία/μνῆσις 'remembrance' or μνήστωρ-class word, or perhaps the end of a damaged compound. Given the chapter's central theme is ⲣ̄ⲡⲓⲙⲉⲩⲉ 'making remembrance' for the deceased catechumen (lines 15, 17), 'remembrance' fits — possibly closing a previous chapter heading or transitioning into the dialogue. Left untranslated to flag uncertainty.

Translated 'in diminishment' rather than 'to diminish.' ⲗⲁⲓ̈ⲟ̄ⲉ = ⲧⲗⲁⲓ̈ⲟ̄ⲉ 'lessening, diminishing' (in glossary) used substantivally with ⲛ̄- as 'in (a state of) diminishment.' Recurs in lines 20, 27 within the cosmic-soteriological framework: the 'other soul' is in diminishment (= captive in sin/body), and the living soul is broadened through the diminishment of the other.

Contracted form of ⲡⲉϩϣⲃⲣ-ⲥⲩⲅⲅⲉⲛⲏⲥ 'his fellow-kinsman' (attested fully in line 2 as ⲡⲉϩϣ[ⲃⲣ]ⲥⲩⲣⲣⲉ[ⲛ]ⲏⲥ). The shortened -ⲉⲛⲟⲥ form appears at lines 9-10 and likely also in segments 5-6. Same referent: the kinsman-soul that intercedes for a captive man, paralleling the Living Soul that intercedes for the catechumen.

The macron-marked ⲡⲣⲉ̄ at line 21 end is ambiguous. Best candidates: (a) ⲡⲣⲏ 'the sun' — fits Manichaean cosmology (light-soul redeemed via sun-ship); (b) ⲡⲣⲉⲛ 'the name' — fits 'redeem in the name of this man.' The continuation [ⲙ]ⲡⲓⲣⲱⲙⲉ 'of this man' on line 22 favors (b). Translated tentatively as 'within the ⲡⲣⲉ̄ of this man'; the precise referent (sun / name / seed) requires parallels.

Verbal form taking ⲛ̄ⲟⲩⲥⲓⲁ 'a substance' as object. Tentative reading as Lyc. reflex of ϣⲱⲣϥ̄/ϩⲱⲣϣ̄ 'spread out, scatter forth' or related distributive verb. Translated 'scatter-forth' provisionally; alternative readings include 'gather' (cf. ⲉⲉⲥⲧϥ̄ in vocabulary) or 'fashion.' The cosmological-soteriological context — the redeeming soul providing/distributing substance to the released catechumen — fits a distributive sense.

Reading ⲁⲣⲁⲧⲏ as ⲁⲣⲉⲧ⸗ⲏ 'at his feet' (cf. ⲧⲏⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧ⸗ in glossary, and accumulated ⲍⲓⲣⲉⲧⲟⲩ 'at their feet'). With ϣⲁⲣⲁϩ = ϣⲁⲣⲟϥ 'to/with him' the phrase suggests the living-relative 'stands at his (the deceased's) feet' (i.e., approaches the Elect on his behalf) and causes the church to make remembrance. Idiomatic for petitioning supervisory presence.

Translated 'I have committed (it) to the hand of you all.' The verbal form ⲁϩ̄ⲧ (with overstroke) appears to be a Lycopolitan perfect-1sg form on a stem of placing/entrusting; combined with the idiom ⲁⲧⲟⲟⲧ⸗ 'into the hand of (someone)' attested elsewhere in the corpus for committing/enjoining (cf. ⲡⲉ†ϩⲱⲛ ⲙ̄ⲙⲁϥ ⲁⲧⲟⲧⲧⲏⲛⲉ in glossary), this gives a sense of formal apostolic entrustment of the catechumens with their soteriological responsibility.

Tentatively rendered 'a concealment'/'a hidden state'. The form ϩⲱⲯ is unusual; possibly Lyc reflex of ϩⲱⲡ 'be hidden, hide' substantivized. Alternative: a form of ⲱⲡ 'reckon, count' giving 'in a reckoning unto the end.' Confidence low.

The 3rd-person prefixes ⲁⲩ- could be either 3pl 'they (his fellow catechumens) blessed/worshipped/glorified' or 3sg.m 'he blessed/worshipped/glorified.' Given that the subject is a single catechumen who heard and responded, I render as 3sg.m ('he'). The Lycopolitan ⲁⲩ- can stand for either.
